A contractor wants to design an entrance sign made up of a rectangle topped by a semicircle, as shown in the diagram. The area of the sign must be $100\,{cm}^{2}.$ What should be the radius $r$ of the semicircle so that the perimeter of the sign is minimized? Do not round the answer.

$r=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{cm}$
question.worked_solution:
We let $r$ be the radius of the semicircle and let $x$ be the height of the rectangle. Then, we want to minimize the perimeter

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =2x+2r+\pi r.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the area is fixed at $100\text{ cm},$ so we also have the constraint condition

$$
100=2rx+\frac{\pi {r}^{2}}{2}.
$$

Now, by making $2x$ the subject of the constraint equation and taking into account that $r>0,$ we find that

$$
\begin{aligned}100 & =2rx+\frac{\pi {r}^{2}}{2} \\ 2rx & =100-\frac{\pi {r}^{2}}{2} \\ 2x & =\frac{100}{r}-\frac{\pi r}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging this into our expression for $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\frac{100}{r}-\frac{\pi r}{2}+2r+\pi r \\  & =\frac{100}{r}+\frac{\pi r}{2}+2r.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to minimize $P,$ so we need to differentiate $P$ and set the derivative equal to zero. Computing the derivative gives

$$
{P}^{′}(r)=-\frac{100}{{r}^{2}}+\frac{\pi }{2}+2.
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{100}{{r}^{2}}+\frac{\pi }{2}+2 & =0 \\ \frac{100}{{r}^{2}} & =\frac{\pi +4}{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{200}{\pi +4} \\ r & =\sqrt{\frac{200}{\pi +4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we confirm that $r=\sqrt{\frac{200}{\pi +4}}$ is a minimum using the second derivative test.

Since the second derivative ${P}^{″}(r)=\frac{200}{{r}^{3}}>0,$ the stationary point 
$r=\sqrt{\frac{200}{\pi +4}}$ is a minimum.
